audit_scope.description: This batch covers: Berlin meta-EIP (EIP-2070), Prague transactional state management, blob base fee reserve price (EIP-7918), alt_bn128 precompile gas reduction (EIP-1108), and Keccak hash functions (crypto/hash module).

misclassified_entities.reason: From EIP-2070: 'Ethereum Network' is the system itself being analyzed. The network is not an external entity crossing a trust boundary.
From EIP-2070: 'EIP Authors' proposing EIPs for Berlin inclusion are governance participants, not runtime external entities interacting with the EL.
From EIP-1108: 'Calling Contract' invoking alt_bn128 precompiles is internal EVM execution via CALL opcode. The precompile call does not cross a trust boundary.

From EIP-1108: 'Untrusted Caller Input' describes data provided by calling contracts. While the data may originate from untrusted transactions, by the time it reaches the precompile it is within EVM execution context, not crossing an external trust boundary.
From crypto/hash: 'Hash Function Caller' is any internal component (transaction validation, state root computation) requesting a keccak256 hash. This is internal to the EL, not an external entity.
From crypto/hash: 'Hash512 Function Caller' is an internal component (e.g., Ethash) requesting keccak512. This is internal to the EL.

From crypto/hash: 'Untrusted Data Source' providing data for hashing is described generically. The hash function itself does not define a trust boundary; the trust boundary is where the data enters the system (P2P, RPC), not where it is hashed internally.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via devp2p (Berlin Fork Blocks)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-2070: peers broadcast blocks over unauthenticated P2P that must be validated against Berlin fork rules after the activation block. Non-upgraded peers will fork off and their blocks must be rejected.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer via P2P (Blob Fee Calculation)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P block propagation with excess_blob_gas header field
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-7918: block producers include excess_blob_gas in block headers. Validators must independently recalculate this value using the modified calc_excess_blob_gas function with reserve price logic. The header value is never trusted and must match the computed value.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via devp2p (Blob Fee Block Validation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-7918: peers propagate blocks with excess_blob_gas values that must be validated using the reserve price conditional logic. Mismatch between computed and header excess_blob_gas causes block rejection.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: devp2p block import -> Fork-Aware Validation -> Berlin Rule Application
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Blocks at or after Berlin activation must be validated against all constituent EIP rules. Blocks from pre-Berlin peers must be rejected post-fork. Fork activation is determined by block number against chain configuration.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P block propagation -> Header Validation -> calc_excess_blob_gas with Reserve Price
boundary_edges.security_assumption: excess_blob_gas must be independently computed using: (1) check if BLOB_BASE_COST * parent.base_fee > GAS_PER_BLOB * blob_base_fee (reserve condition), (2) if true, use reserve mode formula (excess += blob_gas_used * (max - target) / max), (3) if false, use normal formula. Producer-supplied value must match exactly.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: devp2p block import -> excess_blob_gas Recalculation -> Header Comparison
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All clients must implement the reserve price conditional logic identically to maintain consensus. The blobSchedule parameters (target, max) must be correctly loaded from EIP-7840 configuration. Incorrect implementation causes consensus failures.
